def test_test():
    import io
    from contextlib import redirect_stdout

    # test() should evaluate repr() of every 256 characters back to themselves
    # and print nothing when all round-trips succeed.
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(buf):
        test()
    assert buf.getvalue() == "", "test() reported mismatches: %s" % buf.getvalue()

    # Sanity checks of the underlying evalString used by test()
    assert evalString("'\\n'") == "\n"
    assert evalString('"\\t"') == "\t"
    assert evalString("'\\x41'") == "A"
    assert evalString("'\\101'") == "A"
    assert evalString("'''a\\'b'''") == "a'b"
    assert evalString('"plain"') == "plain"

    # Round-trip check mirroring test()'s logic
    for i in range(256):
        c = chr(i)
        assert evalString(repr(c)) == c, "mismatch for %d: %r != %r" % (i, evalString(repr(c)), c)

    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        test()
    # test() prints only when evalString(repr(c)) != c; correct behavior means no output
    assert buf.getvalue() == "", "test() reported mismatches: %r" % buf.getvalue()
